item1.justification: The trace correctly applies §102 anticipation on an element-by-element basis for claims found in single prior art references, and applies Graham/KSR factors (scope and content, differences, PHOSITA level, secondary considerations, motivation to combine) for all §103 rejections, with no conflation of other statutory frameworks.

item2.justification: Every rejection cites specific prior art references (US-2013321456-A1, US-2016247051-A1) and maps particular claim limitations to specific disclosures in those references, such as FIG. 4, Claim 1, and specific features like complexity threshold logic and object-type classification.

item3.justification: Claims 21-22 were found novel at §102 but obvious at §103, with explicit additional rationale provided (HTML5 is industry-standard web technology known to PHOSITA for performance optimization), consistent with the established principle that §103 can reject claims that survive §102 when obviousness is separately justified.

item4.justification: With strictness of 0.818, the examiner consistently resolves all ambiguities toward rejection—including claims with lower confidence (0.7-0.75) on device-type and resolution features—without granting any claims even on borderline evidence, which appropriately reflects the strict gatekeeper profile.

item5.justification: The final rejection decision flows directly and consistently from the accumulated stage analyses: claims found not novel at §102 are rejected under §102, claims found obvious at §103 are rejected under §103, and the two claims found novel but obvious (21-22) receive §103 rejections, with no reversals or unexplained contradictions.
